_comment: Pinned external artefacts for the Agent Friday Windows installer.
Anything listed here is either downloaded by build-installer.ps1 into the
artifact, or downloaded by install.ps1 on the target machine. Anything we
then EXECUTE must carry a sha256 where upstream makes one possible.
Every entry carries a sha256. An empty one refuses: Assert-FileHash stops
setup and Test-FileHash answers no (lib/Download.ps1), so an unpinned file
is never run. tests/unit/test_installer_pins.py keeps it that way.

_why_this_version: 3.12 rather than 3.13: presidio pulls spacy, which pulls blis/thinc/
murmurhash. Those consistently publish cp312 win_amd64 wheels; cp313
coverage lags. 3.12 maximises the chance that every dependency is a wheel.
3.12.10 specifically: it is the LAST 3.12 release with an embeddable
amd64 build. 3.12.11 and later are source-only security releases.
Verified by HEAD request against python.org/ftp on 2026-08-21 - .10, .9
sha256 above was computed from the actual download on 2026-08-21, not
copied from a page. Re-verify if you bump the version.

_why_this_pin: bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py is regenerated in place, so it cannot be
pinned. The same file is published in the pypa/get-pip repository; a
URL at one commit (f6f6441, pip 26.2.1, 2026-08-04) never changes.
sha256 computed from two downloads on 2026-10-21; they matched.
To bump: pick a newer commit of pypa/get-pip, download public/get-pip.py
twice, record the hash and size, and change the commit in the URL.
ollama.com/download/OllamaSetup.exe always serves the latest build and
cannot be pinned. Each GitHub release asset is fixed, and GitHub
publishes its SHA-256 digest; the value above is that digest for

The winget route installs whatever winget's manifest names; winget
checks that installer against the manifest's own SHA-256.
The installer still does not trust Ollama's exit code: after running
it, it goes looking for a working ollama binary.

_comment: There is NO documented silent-install contract for Ollama on Windows.
Upstream issue ollama/ollama#7969 is titled 'Administrative / silent
install is borked'; issue #15038 discusses moving the installer to
NSIS, which would change the switch from /VERYSILENT to /S.
So the installer tries winget first, then each dialect below in order,
and VERIFIES after every attempt by locating and running ollama.exe.
If none of them work it hands the user one clear instruction and lets
setup finish. It never reports Ollama as installed without proving it.
